$comment: HPS-47: a host decides 'is this bundle materialized' from the neutral signals — a non-empty `hosts` object, or a non-empty vector.layers array — never from its own content alone. Every row is a complete MPB 1.0.0 manifest; the host feeds each to its own materialization predicate and asserts the verdict. The other-host and unknown-host rows are the ones that catch a host keying off its own block: they are materialized bundles that carry nothing this host imports. At 1.0.0 the three host-ish signals of the integer era (a known host block, a sibling host block, a dcc_readiness object) are ONE signal, because everything host-specific now lives under `hosts.<hostId>` — a host asks whether the object has any key, never which keys it has.

vectors.name: revit host block only
vectors.note: materialized for someone ELSE is still materialized. A host that answers false here misreads a paid-for bundle as base and tells the user to materialize what already exists.

vectors.name: unknown host, readiness only
vectors.note: the host id is deliberately one no shipped host recognises, and it carries readiness rather than a payload — the `hosts` OBJECT's presence is the signal, which is what absorbs host-roster staleness. This is the 1.0.0 heir of the integer era's `dcc_readiness`-only row: readiness folded into the host block, so the same bundle now signals through `hosts`.

vectors.name: empty vector.layers is no signal
vectors.note: the signal is NON-EMPTY layers; an empty array is base-tier scaffolding

vectors.name: empty hosts object is no signal
vectors.note: the `hosts` twin of the empty-layers row, and new at 1.0.0: collapsing three signals into one makes the container's mere EXISTENCE the tempting shortcut, and an empty object is scaffolding exactly as an empty array is.
